sources.title: Symbolic Analyses of Dataflow Graphs
sources.access: Author-hosted manuscript full text and publisher publication metadata inspected. Manuscript has placeholder journal metadata; publication year verified separately.
sources.passages: Section 2 finite-buffer backward-channel model; Section 4.1 enabling patterns; Section 4.2 symbolic buffer sizing; conclusion.
sources.covers: Symbolic timing/rate performance analysis using execution patterns, exact single-edge buffer/latency formulas and approximate extensions to acyclic graphs.
sources.difference: Finite buffer model inhibits producer firing when space is unavailable; it is not our fixed offered trace with tail-drop and a rejected-plus-late all-offer objective.
sources.claim_implication: Using execution patterns instead of every timing event is established methodology. The differing model does not prove our specialization original.

sources.title: Spotlight Abstraction in Model Checking Real-Time Task Schedulability
sources.access: Full author manuscript uploaded by coauthor Nils Timm inspected. Direct DOI fetch failed in this session; conference page confirms authors/title.
sources.passages: Introduction, Sections 4-6, Algorithms 1-2 and stated schedulability objective.
sources.covers: FIFO/EDF task-queue abstraction with spotlight and shade, iterative timed-automata reachability and fewer task clocks per iteration.
sources.difference: Verifies whether queued tasks meet deadlines; the reviewed passages do not provide a shared-service-parameter finite tail-drop combined-failure extremum algorithm.
sources.claim_implication: FIFO queue state reduction for deadline verification is not new in general.

sources.title: An evaluation of approaches to model checking real-time task schedulability analysis
sources.access: Publisher abstract and introduction preview inspected; full publisher text requires subscription. No artifact run.
sources.passages: Abstract and introduction; explicit continuation of the 2021 spotlight paper.
sources.covers: Separates clock operations from Boolean/integer operations and uses counter abstraction; compares with Timestool and UPPAAL RTLib for FIFO and deadline scheduling.
sources.difference: Schedulability objective and task models differ from exact whole-interval loss-plus-late counts on a fixed finite offer trace.
sources.claim_implication: A practical published abstraction lineage must be distinguished before claiming a new queue verifier or superior scalability.

sources.title: Max-plus-algebraic hybrid automata: Beyond synchronisation and linearity
sources.access: Institution-hosted thesis full text and publication metadata inspected selectively, not every chapter.
sources.passages: Chapter 1 motivation/review; Section 2.4 piecewise-affine/max-min-plus-scaling systems; Section 3.4 guard/reset hybrid model; Chapter 5 parametric models and solvability.
sources.covers: Existing piecewise-affine theory, choice-dependent max-plus hybrid dynamics and parametric event-time models, with solvability and stability analyses.
sources.difference: No ready-made finite tail-drop rejected-plus-late extremum algorithm identified in inspected passages. General modelling machinery could express related transitions; this is an inference, not a proved reduction here.
sources.claim_implication: Choice-sensitive max-plus modelling and parameterized event-time reasoning cannot themselves be claimed new.

sources.title: SMT-Based Reachability Analysis of High Dimensional Interval Max-Plus Linear Systems
sources.access: Author-hosted full text; abstract, model definition and interval semantics inspected. Located through Gupta bibliography reference 176.
sources.passages: Abstract; Section II.B autonomous interval max-plus matrix model, event-varying uncertainty; SMT reachability formulation.
sources.covers: Interval uncertainty in max-plus state matrices and reachability queries encoded in linear real arithmetic for SMT.
sources.difference: Our single service parameter persists across all offers and admissions switch through tail-drop guards. The reviewed formulation is a different system class and reachability objective.
sources.claim_implication: Exact SMT handling of uncertain max-plus models already exists. Our compact Z3 implementation is not a reproduction of this paper.

sources.title: SMT-based and fixed-point approaches for state estimation in max-plus linear systems
sources.access: Author-hosted full manuscript, abstract, Sections 2-3 and conclusion inspected selectively; author publication page confirms April 2025. Found via the Mufid paper search and followed the 2024-to-2025 extension.
sources.passages: Introduction; max-plus fixed-point equations; comparison objective and conclusion.
sources.covers: Bounded-uncertainty state estimation with a concise max-plus fixed-point approach compared with disjunctive SMT; discusses pseudo-polynomial complexity of the fixed-point routine.
sources.difference: Computes feasible state estimates compatible with measurements, not global shared-service-parameter loss/deadline count extrema with tail-drop.
sources.claim_implication: Replacing explicit disjunctions with specialized max-plus computation is an established contribution pattern; our work needs a specific additional result, not merely that general idea.

prior_screen_retained: ../../runtime_io_fifo_admission_step3/20261008-01/sources.json covers max-plus FIFO recurrence, convex-hull pacing, timing observers, quantitative timed automata, lossy FIFO verification and parametric schedulability. Those source assessments are not newly reproduced here.
verdict: No exact ready-made match established in inspected passages; neither an absence proof nor originality established. Practical advantage gate fails against our existing reachable comparator. Broad claims about new uncertainty analysis, FIFO abstraction, max-plus modelling or quantitative optimization are unsupported.
unresolved: Whether admission-pattern-conditioned monotonicity and exact regional combined-failure extrema have an earlier equivalent formulation.
